subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Toughness is best described as a material's ability to:
options: Absorb impact and resist sudden shock without breaking
questions.explain: Toughness is the ability to absorb energy and withstand sudden impacts or shocks without fracturing.

questions.q: A potential divider made from two resistors is used to:
options: Increase the supply voltage above the battery
Provide a fixed lower output voltage from a higher supply
questions.explain: A potential divider uses two resistors to split a supply voltage, providing a smaller, fixed output voltage.

questions.q: A force that squashes or pushes a material together is called:
questions.explain: Compression is a squashing force that pushes material together; tension by contrast pulls it apart.

questions.q: A linkage in a mechanism is used to:
options: Change the direction or type of motion between parts
questions.explain: Linkages are bars connected by pivots that transfer or change the direction and nature of motion in a mechanism.

questions.q: Which process builds an object up layer by layer from a digital model?
questions.explain: 3D printing is an additive process that deposits material layer by layer to build a three-dimensional object directly from a CAD file.

questions.q: Connecting two cells in series rather than one cell will generally:
questions.explain: Cells connected in series add their voltages together, increasing the total supply voltage to the circuit.

questions.q: Which is a natural fibre rather than a synthetic one?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural fibre grown from the cotton plant, whereas polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic fibres made from polymers.

questions.q: One-off (job) production is best suited to making:
options: A single bespoke item such as a tailored wedding dress
questions.explain: One-off production makes a single, often custom item to a unique specification, such as a made-to-measure product.

questions.q: A microcontroller is used in products because it:
options: Only ever works as a battery
Can be programmed to control inputs and outputs flexibly
questions.explain: A microcontroller is a programmable chip that can read inputs and control outputs, allowing one component to perform many control tasks.

questions.q: A first-class lever, such as a seesaw, has the fulcrum positioned:
options: At the same point as the load
Between the effort and the load
Only at the very end of the load
Beyond both the effort and load
questions.explain: In a first-class lever the fulcrum (pivot) sits between the effort and the load, as on a seesaw or pair of scissors.

questions.q: Programming a product's behaviour with a microcontroller rather than fixed wiring is an advantage because:
options: The behaviour can be changed by editing the program without rewiring
It increases the size of the product
It removes the need for any input devices
questions.explain: A programmable microcontroller lets designers change a product's function by altering software, avoiding costly hardware changes.

questions.q: Which property describes a material's ability to be drawn out into a thin wire?
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability of a material to be stretched or drawn into a wire without breaking, a property seen in copper.

questions.q: In a gear train, an idler gear is added mainly to:
options: Change the overall gear ratio of the train
Reverse the direction of the output gear without changing the ratio
questions.explain: An idler gear sits between driver and driven gears to reverse the output's direction; it does not affect the overall gear ratio.

questions.q: Powder coating is a surface finish applied mainly to:
options: Metals, giving a tough durable coloured layer
questions.explain: Powder coating sprays charged powder onto metal which is then baked, forming a hard, durable, attractive finish.

questions.q: The systems approach to electronics describes the order of blocks as:
questions.explain: A system is modelled as input leading to process leading to output, where a signal is received, acted upon, and then produces an action.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between thermoforming and thermosetting polymers?
options: Both can be reheated and reshaped equally
Thermosetting polymers can be reheated and reshaped; thermoforming polymers cannot
Neither type can be shaped by heat
Thermoforming polymers can be reheated and reshaped; thermosetting polymers cannot
questions.explain: Thermoforming (thermoplastic) polymers soften when heated and can be reshaped repeatedly, while thermosetting polymers set permanently and cannot be remelted.

questions.q: A worm gear driving a worm wheel is often used because it:
options: Gives a large speed reduction and high torque in a compact space
questions.explain: A worm and wheel produces a large gear reduction, lowering speed and increasing torque in a small space.

questions.q: Glass-reinforced plastic (GRP), used for boat hulls, is a composite of:
options: Glass fibres set in a polymer resin
questions.explain: GRP combines glass fibres with a polymer resin matrix to create a strong, lightweight, water-resistant composite.

questions.q: Using renewable energy to power a factory mainly helps sustainability by:
options: Reducing carbon emissions and conserving finite resources
Removing the need for any design
questions.explain: Renewable energy lowers carbon emissions and conserves finite fossil-fuel resources compared with burning coal, oil or gas.

questions.q: Choosing FSC-certified timber for a product helps ensure the wood:
questions.explain: The Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certifies timber from responsibly managed, sustainable forests.

questions.q: A product life cycle assessment considers the impact of a product:
options: Only while it is being used
Only at the point of sale
From raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal
questions.explain: A life cycle assessment evaluates environmental impact across the whole life: extraction, processing, manufacture, distribution, use and disposal.

questions.q: PVA and epoxy resin are both types of:
questions.explain: PVA and epoxy resin are adhesives used to bond materials, with epoxy being a strong two-part adhesive.
